best_architecture:
Two-tier containerization for Local-Claw on a RunPod RTX A6000 (48GB) single node.

TIER 1 (production default): Docker Compose v2 as the baseline orchestrator on the single RunPod node. One service per concern: inference-server (Unsloth/Gemma), an optional qwen-fallback service behind a Compose profile, mcp-bridge (TypeScript), python-orchestrator/MCP client, skill-worker(s), mongodb, chroma, redis. Only the inference-server (and qwen-fallback when active) receives the GPU via the modern `deploy.resources.reservations.devices` driver:nvidia spec — NOT the legacy `runtime: nvidia` field. Named volumes isolate durable state: model-cache, mongo-data, chroma-data, redis-data. Service ordering is enforced with healthchecks + `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` so the MCP bridge and workers never connect before the model finishes loading. A single user-defined bridge network gives DNS-based service discovery; env vars referencing other services MUST use the exact compose service name.

TIER 2 (optional migration for autoscaling/HA): k3d (k3s-in-Docker) on the same node. Requires an Ubuntu-based k3s node image (Alpine cannot host the NVIDIA container runtime) plus the k3s arg `--default-runtime=nvidia` so nodes actually advertise `nvidia.com/gpu`. GPU exposure via NVIDIA GPU Operator (or the k8s-device-plugin). Skill-worker autoscaling uses KEDA (queue-depth, scale-to-zero) rather than HPA, since HPA cannot scale to zero and reacts to CPU rather than Redis queue length. Persistence uses local-path-provisioner PVCs (never emptyDir) so model weights survive pod restarts.

Key decision drivers: (1) single-brain GPU policy — never co-resident Gemma + Qwen-32B on 48GB; (2) model weights are large and slow to download, so they must live on a persistent named volume / PVC; (3) the inference server's multi-minute cold start dictates long healthcheck start_period and patient downstream dependencies.
reference_papers:
Containerization/orchestration is primarily an engineering domain rather than an academic one; the authoritative references are specifications and project docs rather than arXiv papers. Closest formal/whitepaper references:
- 'Borg, Omega, and Kubernetes' (Burns et al. 2016) - ACM Queue / CACM - the lineage and design rationale behind Kubernetes scheduling and resource model that k3s/k3d inherit.
- 'Large-scale cluster management at Google with Borg' (Verma et al. 2015) - EuroSys 2015 - foundational resource-reservation and bin-packing concepts mirrored by GPU device-plugin scheduling.
- NVIDIA GPU Operator / device-plugin design notes (NVIDIA, 2023-2025) - vendor whitepapers describing NVML-based discovery and the runtimeClass mechanism underlying `nvidia.com/gpu` advertisement.
No directly relevant arXiv preprints; this field is intentionally light because the SOTA lives in OCI/CRI specs and project documentation, cited under reference_repos.

key_libraries:
Docker Engine (>=24.x) + Docker Compose v2 (>=2.20 for start_interval) - container runtime + Tier-1 orchestration.
nvidia-container-toolkit (>=1.14, requires driver >=525.60.11) - host package enabling GPU passthrough into containers; provides the `nvidia` runtime/CDI.
k3d (v5.7.x) - Go CLI, launches k3s clusters inside Docker for Tier 2.
k3s (bundled by k3d, Ubuntu-based custom node image) - lightweight Kubernetes distribution.
Helm (v3.x) - package manager for installing GPU Operator, KEDA, MongoDB/Redis/Chroma charts.
NVIDIA k8s-device-plugin (v0.17.x) - exposes nvidia.com/gpu resource in Kubernetes.
NVIDIA GPU Operator (latest stable) - automates GPU stack on the cluster.
KEDA (v2.x) - Kubernetes event-driven autoscaler; Redis-list scaler with scale-to-zero.
local-path-provisioner (bundled with k3s) - persistent volume provisioning for model cache.
DCGM Exporter + Prometheus - GPU telemetry/observability (memory pressure, utilization).
pitfalls:
(a) Legacy `runtime: nvidia` in docker-compose.yml. On modern Docker this fails with 'Error response from daemon: unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia' unless the nvidia runtime is manually registered in /etc/docker/daemon.json. CONFIRMED across NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit#150, #194 and IsaacLab#2390. Fix: use `deploy.resources.reservations.devices` with `driver: nvidia` instead. Never mix both methods in one service — they conflict.

(b) k3d default Alpine node image + GPU. Alpine/musl cannot host the NVIDIA container runtime; GPU pods get 'nvidia-smi: command not found' or fail to schedule. Always use an Ubuntu-based k3s node image (88plug/k3d-gpu / cryptoandcoffee/k3d-gpu).

(c) Missing `--default-runtime=nvidia` k3s arg in k3d. CONFIRMED root cause (k3s-io/k3s#4391, #443, #10534, k8s-device-plugin#1228): k3s auto-detects the nvidia containerd runtime but still defaults to runc, so pods start without GPU driver libs. The device plugin then fails with 'Failed to initialize NVML: ERROR_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND' and the node advertises `nvidia.com/gpu: 0` even though `docker exec ... nvidia-smi` works on the node. Fix: pass `--k3s-arg --default-runtime=nvidia@server:*` (and @agent:* if agents exist), or set `runtimeClassName: nvidia` on every GPU pod.

(d) Model weights in emptyDir. emptyDir is wiped on pod delete, forcing a full re-download (tens of GB) on every restart. Use a local-path PVC (Tier 2) or named volume / hostPath (Tier 1).

(e) Co-resident GPU services. Loading Gemma AND Qwen-32B simultaneously on 48GB causes CUDA OOM. Enforce a single-brain policy: put qwen-fallback behind a Compose profile (off by default), set explicit VRAM/resource limits, and never run both concurrently.

(f) No healthcheck on the inference service. The model takes 1-3+ minutes to load; without a healthcheck the MCP bridge and workers start immediately, get connection refused, and enter a cascading restart loop. Fix: add a healthcheck with a generous `start_period` (several minutes) and have dependents use `depends_on: condition: service_healthy`. A `depends_on: service_healthy` pointing at a service with NO healthcheck will also hang forever — the condition is never satisfied.

(g) RunPod nested DinD without `--privileged`. Running k3d inside a RunPod container is nested Docker-in-Docker; NVIDIA device mounts fail unless the outer RunPod container runs privileged with the GPU and required device nodes exposed.

(h) Service-name / env-var drift. If the compose service is renamed but a consumer's connection env var (e.g. MONGO_URI host, INFERENCE_URL) still references the old hostname, DNS resolution fails at runtime with connection-refused. Keep service names and env-var hostnames in lockstep; prefer referencing the canonical compose service name everywhere.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: GPU passthrough into the inference container

  Scenario: Modern device reservation exposes the RTX A6000
    Given infrastructure/docker-compose.yml declares inference-server with deploy.resources.reservations.devices driver:nvidia and capabilities [gpu,utility,compute]
    And NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all and NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility are set on the service
    When the inference-server container starts
    Then running `nvidia-smi` inside the container exits 0 and lists an NVIDIA RTX A6000 with ~48GB memory
    And no "unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia" error appears in the daemon logs

Feature: Patient service ordering around slow model load

  Scenario: MCP bridge waits for the inference model to finish loading
    Given mcp-bridge declares depends_on inference-server with condition service_healthy
    And inference-server has a healthcheck with start_period of several minutes
    When inference-server takes 120s to load the Gemma weights
    Then mcp-bridge is not created until inference-server reports healthy
    And mcp-bridge does not crash-loop with connection-refused during model load

Feature: k3d GPU node advertises GPU capacity (Tier 2)

  Scenario: Cluster created with NVIDIA default runtime advertises a GPU
    Given a k3d cluster created with --gpus all, an Ubuntu-based GPU node image, and --k3s-arg "--default-runtime=nvidia@server:*"
    And the NVIDIA GPU Operator (or device plugin) is installed
    When I run `kubectl describe nodes`
    Then the node capacity and allocatable show `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`
    And the device-plugin pod logs do NOT contain "ERROR_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND"

Feature: Model-weight persistence across restarts

  Scenario: Restarted inference pod reuses cached weights
    Given the inference pod mounts model-cache from a local-path PVC (Tier 2) or the model-cache named volume (Tier 1)
    And the model weights were previously downloaded into that volume
    When the inference pod is deleted and a new pod is scheduled mounting the same volume
    Then the model loads from cache without re-downloading the weights
    And startup time is dominated by load, not download
optimal_implementation:
Scaffold an infrastructure/ folder with the following artifacts. Contents are provided inline and are directly usable.

=== infrastructure/docker-compose.yml (Tier 1, GPU-enabled baseline) ===

services:
  inference-server:
    build: ../services/inference
    image: local-claw/inference:latest
    environment:
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility
      - MODEL_ID=${MODEL_ID:-unsloth/gemma-3}
      - HF_HOME=/models
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/models
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu, utility, compute]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8000/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 300s      # multi-minute model load; failures don't count during this window
      start_interval: 5s      # requires Compose >= 2.20; fast probing during startup
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

  qwen-fallback:
    profiles: ["fallback"]     # OFF by default — single-brain GPU policy; never co-resident with Gemma
    build: ../services/inference
    image: local-claw/inference:latest
    environment:
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility
      - MODEL_ID=${QWEN_MODEL_ID:-Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct}
      - HF_HOME=/models
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/models
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu, utility, compute]
    networks: [local-claw]

  mcp-bridge:
    build: ../services/mcp-bridge
    image: local-claw/mcp-bridge:latest
    environment:
      - INFERENCE_URL=http://inference-server:8000   # MUST match the compose service name
    depends_on:
      inference-server:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

  python-orchestrator:
    build: ../services/orchestrator
    image: local-claw/orchestrator:latest
    environment:
      - MCP_BRIDGE_URL=http://mcp-bridge:9000
      - MONGO_URI=mongodb://mongodb:27017/localclaw
      - CHROMA_URL=http://chroma:8000
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
    depends_on:
      mcp-bridge: { condition: service_started }
      mongodb:    { condition: service_healthy }
      chroma:     { condition: service_healthy }
      redis:      { condition: service_healthy }
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

  skill-worker:
    build: ../services/skill-worker
    image: local-claw/skill-worker:latest
    environment:
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
      - MCP_BRIDGE_URL=http://mcp-bridge:9000
    depends_on:
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

  mongodb:
    image: mongo:7
    volumes:
      - mongo-data:/data/db
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mongosh", "--quiet", "--eval", "db.adminCommand('ping')"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

  chroma:
    image: chromadb/chroma:latest
    volumes:
      - chroma-data:/chroma/chroma
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://localhost:8000/api/v2/heartbeat"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes"]
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    networks: [local-claw]
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  model-cache:
  mongo-data:
  chroma-data:
  redis-data:

networks:
  local-claw:
    driver: bridge

NOTE: no top-level `version:` key — it is obsolete in Compose v2 and emits a warning.

=== infrastructure/scripts/gpu-check.sh ===

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

MIN_DRIVER="525.60.11"

echo "[gpu-check] running nvidia-smi on host..."
if ! command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: nvidia-smi not found on host. Install the NVIDIA driver." >&2
  exit 1
fi
nvidia-smi

DRIVER_VER="$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader | head -n1 | tr -d ' ')"
echo "[gpu-check] detected driver version: ${DRIVER_VER}"
# version compare: lowest of (min, detected) must equal min
if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$MIN_DRIVER" "$DRIVER_VER" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$MIN_DRIVER" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: driver ${DRIVER_VER} < required ${MIN_DRIVER}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "[gpu-check] verifying nvidia-container-toolkit..."
if ! command -v nvidia-ctk >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! dpkg -l 2>/dev/null | grep -q nvidia-container-toolkit; then
  echo "ERROR: nvidia-container-toolkit not installed." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "[gpu-check] verifying GPU passthrough into a container..."
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi >/dev/null \
  && echo "[gpu-check] OK: GPU visible inside container" \
  || { echo "ERROR: GPU not visible inside container" >&2; exit 1; }

echo "[gpu-check] ALL CHECKS PASSED"

=== infrastructure/scripts/setup-cluster.sh (Tier 2: k3d + GPU + KEDA) ===

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

CLUSTER="local-claw"
NS="local-claw"
NODE_IMAGE="ghcr.io/88plug/k3d-gpu:latest"   # Ubuntu-based k3s node image w/ NVIDIA runtime

echo "[setup] preflight GPU check..."
"$(dirname "$0")/gpu-check.sh"

echo "[setup] creating k3d cluster with NVIDIA default runtime..."
k3d cluster create "$CLUSTER" \
  --image "$NODE_IMAGE" \
  --servers 1 \
  --gpus all \
  --k3s-arg "--default-runtime=nvidia@server:*" \
  --port "8000:30080@loadbalancer"

echo "[setup] waiting for node Ready..."
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node --all --timeout=180s

echo "[setup] installing NVIDIA GPU Operator..."
helm repo add nvidia https://helm.ngc.nvidia.com/nvidia >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
helm repo update
helm upgrade --install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator \
  --namespace gpu-operator --create-namespace \
  --set driver.enabled=false   # driver provided by host/node image

echo "[setup] installing KEDA..."
helm repo add kedacore https://kedacore.github.io/charts >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
helm repo update
helm upgrade --install keda kedacore/keda \
  --namespace keda --create-namespace

echo "[setup] creating namespace and deploying manifests..."
kubectl create namespace "$NS" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl apply -n "$NS" -f "$(dirname "$0")/../k8s/"

echo "[setup] verifying GPU advertisement (expect nvidia.com/gpu: 1)..."
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.status.capacity.nvidia\.com/gpu}{"\n"}{end}'

echo "[setup] DONE"

=== infrastructure/scripts/teardown.sh ===

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CLUSTER="local-claw"
echo "[teardown] deleting k3d cluster ${CLUSTER}..."
k3d cluster delete "$CLUSTER" || true
echo "[teardown] pruning dangling docker resources..."
docker system prune -f >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "[teardown] DONE (named volumes / PVC host paths left intact unless manually removed)"

=== infrastructure/k8s/ layout (Tier 2) ===
- namespace.yaml
- inference-deployment.yaml  (resources.limits: nvidia.com/gpu: 1; mounts model-cache PVC; long readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds)
- model-cache-pvc.yaml       (storageClassName: local-path)
- mongodb/, chroma/, redis/  (bitnami/amikos Helm values or plain manifests)
- mcp-bridge-deployment.yaml, orchestrator-deployment.yaml
- skill-worker-scaledobject.yaml  (KEDA ScaledObject: redis list trigger, minReplicaCount: 0, maxReplicaCount: N, pollingInterval: 5, cooldownPeriod: 300)

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
1. RunPod outer container must run privileged with --gpus all for Tier 2 nested DinD; otherwise NVIDIA device mounts fail inside k3d nodes.
2. The inference Helm release can be seeded from vllm-project/production-stack.
3. Every script: `chmod +x infrastructure/scripts/*.sh`.
4. Keep INFERENCE_URL / MONGO_URI / CHROMA_URL / REDIS_URL hostnames in exact lockstep with service names to avoid connection-refused drift.
sota_improvements:
Beyond Gemma's original plan:
- Rootless Docker on RunPod: run the daemon/containers without root to shrink the attack surface (works with nvidia-container-toolkit CDI mode).
- BuildKit cache mounts (`RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip` and the npm equivalent) to slash rebuild times for the Python and TypeScript images.
- Distroless / minimal base images for the production inference container — no shell, far smaller attack surface (keep a debug image variant for troubleshooting).
- Docker Content Trust / image signing (cosign) so only signed Local-Claw images are deployed.
- Compose Watch (`docker compose watch`) for dev-time hot reload of the MCP bridge / orchestrator without full rebuilds.
- CDI (Container Device Interface) instead of the legacy nvidia runtime — the modern, runtime-agnostic GPU-injection path now recommended by NVIDIA.
- vllm-project/production-stack Helm chart as the starting point for the Tier-2 inference release.
- Compose 2.20+ `start_interval` on healthchecks for fast readiness detection during the slow model load.
- DCGM Exporter + Prometheus + Grafana for GPU memory-pressure alerting to enforce the single-brain policy proactively (alert before OOM).
